our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes political orientation the relevant way of standing out.

The plain reading is that substantially differentiating a model's usual political responses is difficult when its training data are shared with competitors, except through special fine-tuning that probably carries an accuracy cost.
Difficulty does not mean impossibility. A likely accuracy cost does not mean every intervention must reduce accuracy.
I use June 1–21, 2025 as the reporting window for the ongoing state described at publication. Earlier experiments provide context unless their findings establish that contemporary state.
The same-data qualification defines the comparison; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled comparisons relevant to the described models show that substantial political differentiation using the same training data generally requires considerable effort without special fine-tuning, and representative evaluations support a probable accuracy cost from the relevant fine-tuning methods.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Repeatable comparisons show that substantial political differentiation is generally straightforward with the same training data and without the excluded fine-tuning methods, or representative evaluations show that the relevant fine-tuning usually preserves accuracy. An isolated successful intervention would not by itself refute a claim of difficulty or probable loss.

evidence.explanation: The study reports political clustering in a German voting-advice setting. This earlier finding does not establish that models used the same data or that differentiation was difficult.

PoliTune describes methods for aligning models with selected political ideologies. Such interventions fall within Marcus's fine-tuning exception; the cited evidence does not establish their probable effect on general accuracy.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled evidence relevant to June 2025 comparing models with shared training data, documenting the effort needed for political differentiation and the accuracy effects of the relevant fine-tuning methods.
